newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Rain hits E.Europe grain crop potential.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Rain hits E.Europe grain crop potential.

text.p: Central and Eastern European farmers face losses of hundreds of thousands of tonnes of grain after widespread flooding, according to government and trade sources in the region.
More rain and flooding is on the way but with crops in many areas already badly hit, the scope for further damage is limited.
Concerns that rain will also hit the quality of grain triggered sharp price rises on the Budapest Commodity Exchange.

This year's Hungarian wheat crop, while almost certain to reach the expected five million tonnes compared with last year's 3.9 million, was likely to be the lowest quality in many years, trader Istvan Grebats of Termin brokerage said.
"We have heard of very bad quality in some places, excellent quality elsewhere, but almost nothing in between," said Gyorgy Pilaszy of trading company Agrograin.
In Poland, steady rain threatened further flooding on Friday.
"It is raining from Koszalin (in the north) through all of western Poland, with varying intensity," flood crisis committee spokesman Krzysztof Pomes said.
"The situation doesn't look good," he told Reuters at 1230 GMT, after several hours of rain in southwestern areas.

Deputy agriculture minister Jerzy Pilarczyk told Reuters in an interview on Thursday that so far 120,000 hectares of grain fields had been destroyed which was likely to cut this year's grain output by 480,000 tonnes.
"The potential new flood wave will affect the same areas already under water," Pilarczyk said.
Rain which hit Yugoslavia in June and July seriously damaged crops on some 200,000 hectares causing a 450 million dinar ($75.8 million) loss, a senior government official said on Friday.

"Heavy rains and hailstorms from June 17 to 20 and in the first (10 days) of July caused enormous damage to crops in Vojvodina and central Serbia," Jan Kisgeci of the federal Agriculture Ministry said.
"The damage is still being evaluated but according to first estimates the loss is some 450 million dinars," he told a news conference.

In the grain growing region of Vojvodina alone some 139,000 hectares were hit by bad weather, or 8.5 percent of total arable land. Wheat was damaged on some 32,000 ha, maize on 61,000 ha and sunflowers on 13 ha.
In Romania recent rains have hit crop quality, an official said on Friday.

"The quality of the wheat harvested over the past week is low. Our wheat might not be in very big demand for export this year," Vasile Duta, general manager of the National Agency for Agricultural Products (ANPA), told Reuters.

The Romanian agriculture ministry expects a total wheat crop of 7.07 million tonnes in 1997, almost double last year's. Duta said heavy rains in recent days had affected crop quality, with gluten content dropping to 74 percent from 83 percent, and increased humidity in the grains.
"These figures are pretty low and very close to standard-wheat quality. They might raise some concerns over milling wheat export prospects," he said.

Rain fell overnight across the flood-swept Czech Republic and storms expected at the weekend could trigger a new wave of the flooding that has devastated parts of the south and east, forecasters said on Friday.

Problems with the weather are not solely the preserve of central and eastern Europe. Grain harvesting in western Europe came to a standstill this week as rain in most producing areas hit crops which had suffered from prolonged spring drought.

Southern hemisphere farmers face potential damage from the developing "El Nino" weather pattern. And CBOT corn futures opened sharply higher in fast trade on Friday on concerns over persistent dry weather in parts of the U.S. midwest.
